By way of above-noted applications, the appellants seek suspension of their sentences during the pendency of their appeals.
2. Since common submissions have been addressed and the impugned judgment is common, the above applications are being disposed of together.

3. The primary contentions raised on behalf of the appellant/Rajiv is that he was not identified by the prosecutrix at the time of her examination wherein she has stated that the offence was committed by another two accused persons.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant/Akram submits that initially in her examination-in-chief the appellant was not identified, however he was later identified only upon his photograph being shown and on the basis of an identifying a mark on the forehead.

5. Learned counsel further submits that version of the incident of the victim as well as eye witness was disbelieved on the aspect of commission of robbery and the appellants stand acquitted for the aforesaid charges vide the impugned judgment.

Per contra, Learned APP for the State, who is duly assisted by counsel for the victim, has opposed the bail applications.
It is contended that the appellants have undergone around 5 years and 4 months out of the total sentence of 20 years.
It is further contended that appellants' acquittal for the offence of robbery was on account of the fact that the initial information about the incident was only of commission of rape.

It is also submitted that at the time of the incident, the victim was accompanied by her brother-in- law, who was examined as PW3, he consistently stated about the PCR call reporting commission of rape by all three appellants.
As per the prosecution case, he was an eyewitness and deposed that all the appellants had committed the offence of rape.
The said witness was also injured in the incident for which the appellants have been convicted for the offence under Section 324 IPC.
Further, the case of prosecution also draws attention to the FSL Report as per which the samples of all three appellants are matched.

Learned APP further draws attention of Rajiv vs State Gnctd Of Delhi on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126227279/
2 the Court to the nominal roll of the appellant/Rajiv as per which, he has been found involved in another case of Section 376(4) IPC in FIR No. 135/2020.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that as per SCRB Report, appellant/Akram is also involved in the said FIR No. 135/2020 which is pending trial.
7. Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances, I find no ground to suspend the sentence of the appellants at this stage and consequently, the above-noted applications are dismissed.
